title: Five minutes
subtitle: to a running engine.
summary: Load Fizlet with one script tag or only the modules you need, start an engine, and give the page back with `destroy()`.
lead: Fizlet is a micro game and animation engine for the DOM: one shared loop, bounded everything, and the page always comes back exactly as it was. The kernel is {size:fizlet (kernel)} gzip ({kb:fizlet (kernel)}), with no runtime dependencies. This page gets an engine running and shows the four calls everything else builds on.

body.text: Pick one. All three ship the same code, built from the same source on every release (v{version} today).

items: **One script tag.** `https://fizlet.com/fizlet.js` puts the kernel and every brick but `fizlet/debug` on `window.fizlet`. No build step. The [quick start](/examples/quick-start.html) runs it as is.

**ES modules, only what you use.** Import each brick from `https://fizlet.com/dist/`: `index.js` is the kernel, `fx.js` is `fizlet/fx`, and so on. A page that imports the kernel and `fizlet/fx` ships only those.

**npm (coming soon).** `npm install fizlet` is not published yet. Until it is: `git clone`, `npm ci`, `npm run build` gives you `dist/` with every subpath export (`fizlet`, `fizlet/fx`, `fizlet/slot` …) and its TypeScript types.
`createEngine({ root, seed })` makes an engine. `root` is the element it lives in: off screen, it pauses. `seed` feeds `engine.random`, so a run replays.
`engine.pool(name, cap, create)` makes every item up front. It never grows: when it is full, `acquire()` says no. That is [contract](/docs/contract/) rule 2.

`engine.add(system)` adds a system with up to four hooks: `read` (measure the page), `step` (simulate, at a fixed 60 Hz), `render` (write the page) and `pause`. [The loop](/docs/loop/) explains the order.
`engine.start()` joins the page's one shared `requestAnimationFrame`. `engine.destroy()` is [Recall](/docs/recall/): every listener goes and every page change is undone.

items.title: The ideas
items.body: Read the [contract](/docs/contract/), then [the loop](/docs/loop/), [Recall](/docs/recall/), [budgets](/docs/budgets/) and [determinism](/docs/determinism/). Each page is short and says which test proves it.

items.title: The bricks
items.body: Input, collision, effects, sprites, sound, timelines, multiplayer and more, each its own import with its own size budget. Every [brick page](/bricks/) lists its whole API from the type declarations.

items.title: A first build
items.body: [Build a micro game](/guides/micro-game/) end to end, or [fill an Astro slot](/guides/astro-slot/) with a hero scene that costs nothing while it is still.

seo.title: Getting started with Fizlet: a DOM game engine
seo.description: Install Fizlet with one script tag or ES modules, start an engine, and give the page back with destroy(). The kernel is under 4 KB gzip, no dependencies.
